findings.F1: The book is mostly the coins' own rise rather than the idea. It held a position on 89 % of the coins' days, and its day returns correlate 0.81 with the coins'. Its Sharpe beats holding's by only 0.05. Its best and worst 2 % of days, +7.2 % and −7.7 %, sit on days when the coins themselves moved +9.4 % and −10.5 %.
findings.F2: The tested falls carry almost nothing. Per case the unusual move is +0.10 % over 3 days (t 0.43, 1471 days), which is 0.5 times the 0.19 % cost of a trade. Only the deepest decile of falls in daily-volatility units (below −1.06) shows a rebound: +0.13 of a usual 3-day move, t 1.60, 472 grid bars. The other nine deciles are flat, between −0.05 and +0.02.
findings.F3: Long up-streaks are followed by further rises, but not beyond chance once every angle is counted. At 7 days the up-streak-length slope has t 2.20 (2443 grid bars), and 5+ up closes are followed by +0.36 of a usual move (t 1.96, n 58). At 3 days the same group shows +0.23 (t 2.51, n 131). Down streaks show no mirror: the slope t is −1.81 at 7 days and 0.21 at 3 days.
findings.F4: The past 7-, 14- and 30-day volatility-scaled return gives a weak positive slope on the next 3 to 10 days. The t values run 1.14 to 2.09, and only one of nine passes 2 (7-day return on 10-day horizon, t 2.09, 1403 grid bars). By coin, the 7-day/3-day t runs from −0.95 for LTC to 2.29 for XRP. The two halves of the windows give t 0.39 for w1–w12 and 1.20 for w13–w24.
findings.F5: Several other angles show nothing that stands out:

no_ideas: Across about 60 angles (streaks, scaled returns of 1 to 30 days, horizons of 3 to 10 days, volatility, range, close location, weekday, coin and window halves), no pattern reached a t that stands out from chance; the up-streak and 7-to-30-day momentum readings (F3, F4) cluster near t 2, are unstable by coin and by half of the windows, and their per-case size is too small against the 0.19 % cost to justify a new idea.
